text:
jordan: Heads up — noticed a jump in billed token counts for a small cohort after the route-mux v2 rollout. Dashboard shows +12% across 3 tenants since 02:00 UTC :eyes:
maya: Ugh. Is that real usage or duplicate events from the aggregator?
sam: I saw a similar spike in transport retries yesterday. Could be backpressure causing double-emits from the ingest shim.
jordan: Metering view looks like duplicate event ids with same request_id but different shard. Example log:```json
{"ts":"2026-03-18T02:12:09Z","req_id":"r-4f7a","shard":"s1","tokens":42}
{"ts":"2026-03-18T02:12:09Z","req_id":"r-4f7a","shard":"s2","tokens":42}
```
lee: That log pattern would cause the aggregator to count both shards if the dedupe key isn't normalized to req_id+tenant. Did the mux change shard keys?
maya: Route-mux v2 added a hashed shard_key for affinity. I thought we normalized to trace_id before forwarding. Seems we missed the dedupe pre-step for the metering path.
metering-bot: alert: billing-delta-high for tenants: tenant-alpha, tenant-gamma (delta +11.7% over 1h). Investigating run_id=mv-20260318-02
sam: Confirmed: route-mux v2 emits shard_key header x-route-shard: hash(tenant,session) and we forward the raw headers into the metering stream. Old mux used fixed header x-session-id. Deduper expects x-session-id, not the new hash.
jordan: So deduper can't collapse duplicates because key changed. Can we map hash -> session id upstream?
lee: Quick mitigation: add a transform in the ingest sidecar to rewrite x-session-id = headers['x-session-id'] || headers['x-route-shard'] with a prefix so deduper sees consistent key. Patching now to canary in us-west-2.
maya: Can we instead update the deduper to canonicalize both keys? That seems safer long-term but takes longer.
sam: Agree. Short-term sidecar rewrite is fastest. Long-term: deduper should accept multiple candidate keys and prefer canonical_session when present.
ops-bot: deploy started: sidecar-rewrite-canary -> us-west-2 (deployment id: dpl-7832)
jordan: FYI console shows invoice preview noise — customers will see inflated previews until backfill runs. We should pause invoice preview generation for affected tenants until dedupe fix completes. Thoughts?
lee: Pause previews for affected tenants only, yes. We can set a preview-exclude flag per tenant in billing-config service. I'll open a quick PR.
maya: Also need to mark the anomaly in the dashboard: add a tooltip explaining "route-mux rollout change caused duplicate event ids; preview suppressed". Otherwise SRE will burn cycles.
sam: Long-term note: rollout UX should require metering compatibility test. Add a step to the rollout checklist: "verify header mappings and dedupe key compatibility with billing pipeline".
jordan: Agreed. Also add a small telemetry gauge in the console that shows dedupe-rate and duplicate-token-count per tenant. Could be a single-line card next to token usage.
lee: I'll sketch the card in the console ticket (console#4721).
metering-bot: status: sidecar-rewrite-canary healthy after 3 min; duplicate-rate dropped from 8% -> 0.6% in canary traffic.
jordan: Nice. Roll forward to all regions after 10m stable.
ops-bot: deploy success: sidecar-rewrite -> global (dpl-7832).
maya: I've opened deduper backlog item to accept both keys and to add unit tests (ingest-dedupe#129).
sam: We'll kick a backfill job to dedupe already ingested duplicates and reconcile invoice previews. Backfill job id: bf-20260318-09
jordan: Assigning follow-ups: lee (pause previews + console tooltip), maya (deduper backlog), sam (backfill + audit report), I'll draft postmortem note for the rollout checklist change.
lee: On it. PR up in 15.
maya: Triage done. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
jordan: Wrapping — will post a short blurb in #product-notices for any affected customers once backfill completes.
